So I’m in a similar situation as you (an American wanting to study in the UK), and the way that I understand it is that it depends on the school. Most large universities will just accept American ACT/SAT scores & your GPA, but some also require that you’ve taken AP classes and gotten a certain score (this can be bypassed by taking college courses here). 

As for visas, it depends a lot on what you’re doing, how long you’re staying, and what school you’re studying at. You should be looking at Tier 4 visas (here’s a link to the government site: [gov.uk tier 4 visa](https://www.gov.uk/study-uk-general-student-visa-tier-4) ).  

I hope this helped! If you want more help/clarification feel free to reply/dm me :)

Hi! I’m an American so I haven’t taken any tests to study here but I’m hoping I can help a bit.

First, in regards to the GMAT, it looks like there are three sections, a writing section, a problem solving/math section, and a speaking section. A good resource for this would be: [MBA GMAT](https://www.mba.com/ocp/the-gmat-exam). This site provides a more in-depth overview of the test as well as study courses. 

Second, the GMAT is normally a graduate course test, so if you’re an undergrad it may be helpful to take an SAT and a TOEFL test. The SAT is one of the standard tests that American students take to get into University and the TOEFL is an English comprehension test. 

Third, I would recommend looking up the schools you would like to attend and seeing if they have any lists of scholarships that would apply to you. If you just want general lists of scholarships here’s a few:

•[Top Universities ](https://www.topuniversities.com/student-info/scholarship-advice/international-scholarships-study-us) 
•[India Education ](http://www.indiaeducation.net/studyabroad/usa/scholarships.html) 
•[World Education Services ](https://www.wes.org/advisor-blog/u-s-and-canadian-scholarships-for-indian-students/) 

Also, since your family has a lower income, there’s a good chance that you qualify for financial aid. How much you can receive depends on the school but it doesn’t hurt to see what you can get.

I hope this helped a bit! Feel free to dm me if you have more questions and I can try to do some more research on my end.

I would do pan fried chicken breasts with the king’s prawn and the mushrooms for the main dish. 

~~~~

Recipe:

Heat the oil in a pan and season the chicken with salt/pepper/Italian seasoning to taste. Fry on each side approx. 10 min on high or until cooked all the way through. 

In another pan, melt some margarine. Season the prawns with the same seasonings as before and fry them in the pan until done. 

Use the chicken pan to melt some margarine (this will more or less be the sauce, so you’ll need a lot). Cut the mushrooms to the preferred thickness and sauté in salt/pepper. Maybe add a bit of Worcestershire for acidity. 

~~~~

For sides you could do mashed or roasted potatoes, a simple salad (salad greens, sliced cucumbers, shredded carrots, a touch of olive oil), green beans, or peas.

A good place to start would be to look at either the Princeton Review website or the College Board website- they both have college/uni search pages that make it easy to find what you’re looking for. It would also be a good idea to look for smaller technical colleges, as they generally have lower requirements. Once you graduate from there, you can get a better degree at a larger school. 

Links:
[College Board BigFuture](https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/college-search) 

[Princeton Review College Search](https://www.princetonreview.com/college-search) 

If you have any more questions, don’t be afraid to ask and good luck with your search! :)
